topics.title: John Milton: the poet and his life

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and interpret the key facts of Milton's life, education, blindness and late works given in the introduction.

topics.title: On Time: the race of Time and what it devours

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the images of envious Time, the leaden-stepping hours and the plummet's pace.
Interpret why the loss to humans and the gain to Time are both said to be little.

topics.title: On Time: Eternity and the triumph over Time

concepts.learning_objective: Identify what is associated with the eternal and what guides the soul to the supreme Throne.
Evaluate who finally wins the race against Time and why.

topics.title: On Shakespear: no need of a monument of stone

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Milton calls a stone monument a 'weak witness' of Shakespeare's name.
Interpret how the readers' wonder becomes Shakespeare's live-long monument.

topics.title: On Shakespear: the reader's tribute and the poet's art

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Shakespeare's 'easie numbers' and 'Delphic lines' inspire succeeding generations.
Analyse the paradox of readers turned to marble forming a tomb kings would die for.
Define etymology and read the origin note given in a dictionary entry.
Recall the facts about French borrowings into English given in the chapter.
